findings.premise: The persisted row design specifies the information required upstream for lineage and processing outcomes.
findings.evidence: The requirements specify revision 'predecessor, mutation reason, source event and normalizer/prompt/schema versions' and receipt 'affected memory revisions' and 'processing version'. HLD requires full schemas in the owning LLD. S003 specifies the shared Arrow envelope but leaves per-kind payloads descriptive; these required fields and their validation contracts are not defined. Existing public types provide no replacement: MemoryCommand.payload is Json and OperationReceipt contains only minimal public status. findings.action: Define the persisted discriminated payload schemas, required lineage/outcome fields, lifecycle statuses and legal transitions. Separate S3 storage validation from S4 semantic interpretation.

findings.premise: The existing foundation supports durable admission/status but has no authoritative memory store or public semantic reads.
findings.evidence: MemoryFactory.open currently acquires ownership, starts FileQueue and constructs EmbeddedMemoryService with [queue]. The service forwards submit/operation to ingress; context, search and inspect each reject NOT_READY. Inspection of the package implementation found no existing store implementation. findings.action: Preserve explicit unavailable read behavior during S3.

findings.premise: The recorded Lance probe establishes basic compatibility, not crash durability or platform parity.
findings.evidence: The probe exercises one mixed-row merge, a pinned reader, refresh and clean close/reopen. Its report explicitly states 'Small normal-exit macOS probe only' and 'No crash/fsync, Linux, concurrent-reader-under-kill or power-loss qualification'. The design accurately preserves these limitations. findings.action: Keep native crash and Linux qualification as outstanding mandatory build gates.

findings.premise: S2 already exposes the receipt-verification port and retained-identity protections S3 proposes to reuse.
findings.evidence: ReceiptVerifier defines byIdentity, byOperation and optional confirmRetirement. TerminalProof carries the stated identity/hash/scope/epoch/generation/receipt fields and queueTerminal:true. FileQueue.persist checks an authoritative receipt against both the retry and any retained accepted entry; markResolved verifies proof before checkpoint publication. Retirement requires confirmation against retained digests. findings.premise: The installed SDK exposes the merge, version-pinning and ordered-query primitives required by the proposed approach.
findings.evidence: Installed 0.40.0 implements mergeInsert update/insert builders and schema-based execute; Table exposes version, checkout and checkoutLatest; query exposes orderBy. These support the proposed API usage, while native atomicity and resource bounds remain qualification work. The live [SDK reference](https://lancedb.github.io/lancedb/js/classes/MergeInsertBuilder/) differs from installed naming, so installed-version qualification matters. findings.premise: The lifecycle contract completely specifies how the new store joins existing service shutdown and failed-startup cleanup.
findings.evidence: EmbeddedMemoryService manages resources through OwnedWork: stopAdmission(), pending(), drain() and close(). The proposed MemoryStore exposes only close() among those methods. Current host-node startup cleanup closes only queue before owner.close(). The LLD promises drained store work and retained ownership but does not specify the OwnedWork adapter, participant ordering or cleanup of a store opened before queue startup fails. findings.action: Specify the host composition adapter and shutdown ordering, including pending native writes/read leases and store cleanup when queue startup fails. Identify any runtime changes needed.

findings.premise: Existing queue-only directories are preserved rather than silently adopted with an empty receipt authority.
findings.evidence: Current host composition creates queue-only roots. S2's receipt barrier explicitly refuses reopening recycled queues without authoritative retirement support. S003 distinguishes pristine initialization from existing queue-only roots, refuses automatic replacement, preserves queue bytes and assigns migration to S9. This preserves S2's replay-authority requirement. findings.premise: S3 remains within the authoritative-store boundary and preserves adjacent story ownership.
findings.evidence: HLD assigns S3 physical encoding, receipt lookup, atomic commit, revision and tombstone guards. The LLD leaves semantic reconciliation to S4, ranking/public reads to S5, delivery semantics to S8 and migration/purge to S9. Existing public contracts remain compatible with the proposed private additions, and no backend database handle or model-provider implementation enters the package. findings.action: Keep delivery unavailable and avoid implementing migration, ranking or semantic processing in this story.

findings.premise: The proposed uncertain-write and commit-before-ACK handling is compatible with existing queue failure semantics.
findings.evidence: S2 readReceipt converts unavailable or malformed proof into ReceiptUnavailableError, never absence. FileQueue preserves pending entries until verified markResolved; receipt lookup does not silently ACK them. S003 fences uncertain native writes, retains ownership until settlement, reconciles receipts before effects and releases its lane before queue ACK. These rules address the actual queue-to-store dependency without introducing a reverse callback. findings.action: Exercise these paths with the planned real Lance child-process tests; existing fake receipt tests establish only the queue contract.

findings.premise: The ac3 mapping covers the complete upstream store-separation acceptance criterion.
findings.evidence: AC-29 requires index reset/rebuild to preserve memory, memory reset/cleanup to preserve index data and pending events, and refusal of unsafe overlapping cleanup paths. DEF ac3 retains the reset/rebuild requirement. S003 maps ac3 to directory-separation/no-empty-replacement and packaging tests, but specifies only an independent index sentinel fixture; it does not define the bidirectional reset/rebuild or overlap-refusal scenarios. The real index rebuild performs destructive repository deletion, so path separation alone is not the complete oracle.
